liu2024scalable: Implicit GNNs capture long-range dependencies well, but full-batch training and the many iterations needed to solve the fixed-point equation make them expensive on large graphs. SEIGNN combines a mini-batch training scheme that adds coarse-level nodes so global, long-range information still reaches each batch, with a stochastic solver that obtains unbiased approximate solutions in fewer iterations. Across large graphs it outperforms implicit-GNN baselines with higher accuracy and shorter training time, showing that implicit message passing can scale beyond small graphs.
yao2025who: Multimodal retrieval-augmented generation is sensitive to the order in which evidence is shown, and performance becomes unstable as more items and modalities are retrieved. Controlled experiments across text-only, image-only, and mixed-modality tasks reveal a consistent U-shaped accuracy curve over evidence position. A Position Sensitivity Index and attention-layer visualizations quantify the effect: multimodal interaction amplifies position bias relative to unimodal settings, and the bias grows logarithmically with retrieval range. The findings motivate evidence reordering and debiasing strategies for reliable, fair RAG.
